## Before class: bring something inspectable

[The flip · 15–20 minutes using existing work]{.kicker}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.activity-card}
[Share your review packet]{.card-title}

- one decision or research claim
- one actual drawing, result or comparison
- its criterion, metric/rule and source
- the exact file/page behind the claim
- one limitation and one question
:::
::: {.concept-card}
[Read your classmate's packet]{.card-title}

Choose the **Research** or **Studio** prompts on the [practice card](../templates/peer-review-card.qmd).

Write one readback, one evidence-linked challenge and one feasible check. Mark missing evidence as missing.
:::
::::

Rough A3/A4 material is enough. Share early enough for the other student to inspect it; use Slack or a local file exchange.

::: {.notes}
The instructor reads both packets. If preparation is missing, use the published case first, then assemble the packet in the preparation block. The A3 brief states end of Week 9 only; do not infer a calendar deadline from this deck. Real paper forms and source editions are collected in the source pack, checked 18 November 2026.
:::

## Session 1: real requirements, then your work

[50 minutes · two students and the instructor]{.kicker}

| Time | Activity | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5 | Identify the A3 → A4 claim | One reviewable decision |
| 5–20 | Compare real forms, measurements and studio requests | Know what each review asks for |
| 20–30 | Inspect one published paper case | One bounded judgment and request |
| 30–40 | Inspect the other student's packet | A draft review card |
| 40–50 | Clarify the criterion and missing evidence | One feasible check |

::: {.takeaway}
Session 2 turns the critique into a revision and a recheck of your own work.
:::

::: {.notes}
The source pack is a reference, not additional required lecture content. Introduce both paper cases briefly; choose one for the ten-minute exercise. Use the studio report to demonstrate an actual reviewer request, then select the prompts relevant to each student's project. Preserve the peer-inspection time.
:::

## A3 supplies evidence; A4 makes it usable

| Existing material | Reviewer asks | A4 destination |
|---|---|---|
| A1 decision + A2 method | Why this choice and comparison? | Practice Case + Research Brief |
| A3 output and failures | What does the result actually support? | Object Card + Research Brief |
| Files and checks | Can someone trace or reproduce it? | Reproducibility Capsule |
| Feedback and response | What changed, and why? | Feedback + Revision Ledger |
| Remaining limits | What can transfer? | Reflection Note |

::: {.source-note}
[A4 brief: six required components](../assignments/assignment-04.qmd). Today we inspect rough fragments; a complete package is not required yet.
:::

---

## Four things that should never be one score

| Item | What it tells you | What to record |
|---|---|---|
| **Study metric** | A measured or computed property | Definition, units, baseline and conditions |
| **Decision rule** | What triggers a project action | Threshold/comparison and its authority |
| **Reviewer rating** | A judgment under a particular venue's criteria | Scale, reason and confidence/expertise |
| **A4 grade** | Achievement under the course rubric | Published criteria and weights |

::: {.takeaway}
A better metric does not automatically mean a better building—or an acceptable paper.
:::

---

## Three actual forms ask different things

[Published reviewer requirements · selected fields]{.kicker}

| Venue | Reviewer task | What the form produces |
|---|---|---|
| **NeurIPS 2026** | Assess the contribution on separate dimensions | Ratings, actionable questions and confidence |
| **ACM CHI 2026** | Explain the HCI contribution and necessary changes | Recommendation plus a revision list |
| **PLOS ONE** | Check technical validity and support for conclusions | Structured answers with explanatory comments |

::: {.ask-room}
Would the same evidence answer all three sets of questions?
:::

::: {.source-note}
Actual forms and scales: [source pack](../templates/reviewer-source-pack.qmd#real-review-forms). These are named editions, not a universal review rubric.
:::

---

## NeurIPS: a rating needs a reason

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.concept-card}
[Actual 2026 form]{.card-title}

- four dimension ratings: **1–4**
- overall recommendation: **1–6**
- reviewer confidence: **1–5**
- ideally **3–5 actionable questions**
:::
::: {.activity-card}
[Our short practice]{.card-title}

Choose one consequential question.

**What answer would change your advice?**

Name the evidence you need and why it matters to the contribution.
:::
::::

::: {.source-note}
[NeurIPS 2026 handbook, Review Form](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/MainTrackHandbook#review-form). Full dimension names and scale meanings are in the [source pack](../templates/reviewer-source-pack.qmd#real-review-forms). Do not average these into one validity score.
:::

---

## CHI and PLOS: specify the missing evidence

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.concept-card}
[CHI · contribution and revision]{.card-title}

The actual form asks for a **clear list of revisions**.

**Our prompt:** Which correction is needed for this contribution to be supported? How could you check that it was made?
:::
::: {.concept-card}
[PLOS ONE · validity]{.card-title}

The actual form asks whether the method is sound and the conclusions follow from the data.

**Our prompt:** Which claim can you verify from a specific result, regardless of how exciting the topic sounds?
:::
::::

::: {.source-note}
[CHI 2026 form](https://chi2026.acm.org/guide-to-a-successful-submission/#the-review-form) · [PLOS ONE form, p. 1](https://genweb.plos.org/Marketing/plosone-reviewer-form.pdf). Classroom prompts are adaptations, not quotations from reviewers of the following papers.
:::

## Real paper A: improving which output?

[House-GAN++ · Nauata et al., CVPR 2021 · Table 2]{.kicker}

| Dynamic refinement target | FID ↓ | Graph-edit distance ↓ |
|---|---:|---:|
| FID (paper’s diversity proxy) | 24.7 ± 0.8 | 3.7 ± 0.0 |
| Compatibility | 35.7 ± 1.3 | 2.6 ± 0.0 |

**FID:** distance between generated/reference image-feature distributions; unitless. **Graph-edit distance:** mismatch between requested and reconstructed room/door graphs. Lower is better for both.

::: {.takeaway}
The target changes which metric improves. Neither column measures every architectural requirement.
:::

::: {.source-note}
[Published Table 2, p. 13639](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/papers/Nauata_House-GAN_Generative_Adversarial_Layout_Refinement_Network_towards_Intelligent_Computational_Agent_CVPR_2021_paper.pdf#page=8). Mean ± SD across five rounds; 1,000 layouts per round. Exact model/target labels and reading task: [case A](../templates/reviewer-source-pack.qmd#case-a-layout-generation-which-metric-is-being-improved).
:::

---

## Real paper B: what does the threshold justify?

[Mora & Bardhan · Cambridge retrofit study · 2025]{.kicker}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.example-card}
[Reported result]{.card-title}

**18 of 25** cases were classified as having higher retrofit need using the study's wall **ΔT >2°C** criterion.

This is a screening rule from this study, not a general building standard.
:::
::: {.warning-card}
[Inspect before transferring it]{.card-title}

What temperatures define ΔT? Why that cutoff? Would a different heating condition alter the classification?

The authors acknowledge unknown thermostat/occupancy conditions and limited sampling.
:::
::::

::: {.source-note}
[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsos.241337), §2.2.3, §3.1.3/Figure 6 and §4.4; [open PDF and reading task](../templates/reviewer-source-pack.qmd#case-b-thermal-images-what-does-a-screening-threshold-establish). These are our review questions, not published reviewer comments.
:::

## Studio review: an actual request for evidence

[Pier Pavilion redevelopment, Llandudno · DCFW review · August 2020]{.kicker}

**Problem identified:** the submitted text and drawings did not make the proposed changes clear enough to assess.

**Actual reviewer request:** a revised Design and Access Statement with side-by-side comparisons of the consented and proposed schemes—covering residential units, retail area and access.

::: {.activity-card}
**Our transfer:** put two versions of your project beside each other. Mark what changed, then show the spatial consequence that the reviewer needs to judge.
:::

::: {.source-note}
[Actual review letter, 24 August 2020, p. 2, items 4–5](https://dcfw.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/PierPavilionLLandudnoSection73DeskTopEnquiry2482020.pdf#page=2). We use its evidence request; the planning-procedure discussion is outside this exercise.
:::

## What does a real design panel ask to see?

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.concept-card}
[Mid Sussex · published criteria]{.card-title}

Architectural integrity · context · environmental performance · character · detail.

The panel gives advice; its review is not a planning decision.
:::
::: {.concept-card}
[DCFW · submission requirements]{.card-title}

Brief, site analysis, plans, sections and elevations.

**Our task:** trace one site observation or design intention to a visible decision in those drawings.
:::
::::

::: {.source-note}
[Mid Sussex terms, 2018, p. 1](https://www.midsussex.gov.uk/media/1579/design-review-panel-terms-of-reference.pdf) · [DCFW Essentials, 2020](https://dcfw.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DCFW-DR-Essentials-2020-Eng.pdf). UK review examples, not Hong Kong regulations or A4 weights.
:::

---

## Studio track: ask, inspect, then advise

[Course-curated questions · choose one row]{.kicker}

| Focus | Question | Evidence to open |
|---|---|---|
| Context | Which site condition changed the design? | Site analysis + affected plan/section |
| Integrity | Where do use, circulation and structure conflict? | Coordinated drawings |
| Environment | What improves against which alternative? | Comparable runs + assumptions |
| Character | Where does the concept become spatial? | Diagram + drawing consequence |
| Detail | Which interface could undermine the intent? | Relevant junction/material detail |

::: {.takeaway}
Advance this aspect, revise it, or request evidence—with a located reason and a checkable next action.
:::

::: {.source-note}
[Studio track: adequacy checks and real sources](../templates/reviewer-source-pack.qmd#studio-track). These questions and course actions are adaptations. Qualitative judgments need evidence; they do not need an invented numerical cutoff.
:::

## Review one published result in ten minutes

[Choose case A or B · open the source pack]{.kicker}

| Time | Do this | Write |
|---|---|---|
| 0–3 · alone | Locate the table/sections and metric definition | One supported statement and its scope |
| 3–7 · compare | Identify a missing check or consequential disagreement | One evidence-linked question |
| 7–10 · together | Specify the evidence or correction needed | One request and what would change your advice |

::: {.activity-card}
**A:** Which metric would guide your decision, and which spatial quality still needs checking?

**B:** Does this result justify investigation, a diagnosis, or a design action? What further evidence distinguishes them?
:::

::: {.source-note}
[Paper track: exact reading locations](../templates/reviewer-source-pack.qmd#paper-track). Judge the inspected claim; a short excerpt does not justify a whole-paper accept/reject verdict.
:::

## Now inspect your classmate's work

[Session 1 · 30–50 minutes · following slides are references]{.kicker}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.concept-card}
[Locate the concern]{.card-title}

Point to the result and the claim it supports.

Is the issue a missing definition, an unfair comparison, an untested condition or a claim beyond the evidence?
:::
::: {.activity-card}
[Specify completion]{.card-title}

Request a clarification, a feasible check or a narrower statement.

**“I could reconsider when I can inspect ___.”**
:::
::::

A missing item in your reading is not automatically an error in the paper. Check whether it appears elsewhere; acknowledge limits the authors already state.

::: {.takeaway}
Start ten minutes of silent inspection now. Then spend ten minutes clarifying the criterion and next check with the author.
:::

## Transfer the review to your own A3/A4 work

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.concept-card}
[Research track]{.card-title}

Choose one result and its contribution claim.

Inspect the method, metric definition, comparator and test conditions. State what can be concluded and what check could change that conclusion.
:::
::: {.concept-card}
[Studio track]{.card-title}

Choose one spatial or environmental decision.

Inspect the relevant drawing/output and its consequence. Recommend a change or comparison, with evidence needed to judge it.
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
Both tracks end with a review of the student's own work and one revision or check for A4.
:::

## A4 criteria: inspect the argument

**Project criteria** judge the design options. **A4 criteria** judge the quality of the argument and workflow.

| Criterion · course weight | Reviewer question | Inspect |
|---|---|---|
| Decision clarity · 15% | What choice, for whom, between which alternatives? | Decision sentence and alternatives |
| Workflow execution · 20% | What changed between runs? | One input → operation → output chain |
| Evidence and uncertainty · 20% | What could reverse the conclusion? | Metric, rule source and sensitivity |
| Design impact · 15% | What changes in the design? | Drawing, selected option or next action |

::: {.source-note}
[A4 assessment criteria](../assignments/assignment-04.qmd#assessment-criteria). These are course weights; classmates do not award marks.
:::

---

## A4 criteria: inspect the handoff

| Criterion · course weight | Reviewer question | Inspect |
|---|---|---|
| Reproducibility · 15% | Can someone reproduce the key result? | Inputs, file, instructions and expected output |
| Revision judgment · 10% | What did critique change, and why? | One feedback → response → revision link |
| Communication · 5% | What is clear without narration? | Figure/card read silently, then restated |

Reference during inspection: choose **two A4 criteria** for detailed review. Always flag an unsupported main claim or missing runnable artifact.

::: {.grading-note}
These criteria apply to your A4 work. They do not grade the published papers or replace a venue's review form.
:::

## Prepare your classmate's review

[Session 1 · 30–50 minutes]{.kicker}

**First 10 minutes:** inspect the packet silently. Complete one record on the [practice card](../templates/peer-review-card.qmd): question/rule, expected result or feature, actual observation/location, judgment and next check.

**Next 10 minutes:** clarify terms or files with the author and instructor. Record any disputed threshold or interpretation.

::: {.activity-card}
“I understand your decision to be ___. The result supports ___ under ___. My main question is ___ because ___.”
:::

Choose a check that can be attempted in the 18-minute repair block. Record a larger investigation as a next step.

---

## The card records what you actually inspected

| Field | Record |
|---|---|
| **Measure or inspect** | A defined metric, visible feature, source or workflow step |
| **Comparison + conditions** | Baseline/rule and its source; test conditions or intended spatial relationship |
| **Observation** | What you found, with exact file/figure/cell/run |
| **Judgment** | What the result supports; whether the evidence is adequate |
| **Next action** | What to check/change and what would resolve the concern |

::: {.takeaway}
Use an actual value or located observation. Missing evidence is a finding, not a number to fill in.
:::

::: {.source-note}
[Practice card: inspection record](../templates/peer-review-card.qmd#your-inspection-record). One complete record is enough for the class review.
:::

---

## Judge the result and the evidence separately

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.concept-card}
[Result or design]{.card-title}

If a stated rule applies: **meets / does not meet / cannot yet judge**.

If no target rule applies: mark **not applicable** and explain the qualitative finding.
:::
::: {.concept-card}
[Evidence]{.card-title}

**Supported within checked scope / problem found / not established**.

State what you checked and what you did not check.
:::
::::

An option can miss a target while the analysis is sound. A passing number can rest on an unchecked model. A qualitative judgment can be well supported without a numerical score.

::: {.source-note}
These are course working labels, not journal ratings. [Definitions on the practice card](../templates/peer-review-card.qmd#judge-the-design-result-and-evidence-separately).
:::

---

## Session 2: review, act, recheck

[50 minutes · two students and the instructor]{.kicker}

| Time | Activity | Save |
|---|---|---|
| 0–12 | B leads the review of A's work | Review card + author's response |
| 12–24 | A leads the review of B's work | Review card + author's response |
| 24–42 | Each author performs one check or revision | Revised result, or exact blocker |
| 42–47 | Peer recheck: 2½ minutes per project | Supported claim and remaining gap |
| 47–50 | Record the response and next action | Dated A4 ledger entry |

The instructor checks evidence, clarifies disagreements and supports both repairs. Each student acts as reviewer and author.

---

## Each review takes 12 minutes

| Time | Lead | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 0–3 | Reviewer | Read back the claim; locate evidence; explain one challenge |
| 3–5 | Author | Correct misunderstandings and supply context |
| 5–8 | Both | Inspect one link or discuss the proposed test |
| 8–10 | Reviewer | Recommend an action and completion evidence |
| 10–12 | Author | Accept, adapt, defer or reject the advice, with a reason |

::: {.takeaway}
End with a defensible next action, not a list of preferences.
:::

::: {.notes}
For one student, the instructor supplies an example packet and takes the second role. For three students, use three eight-minute reviews in the same 24-minute block: two-minute readback, one-minute clarification, two-minute challenge, two-minute advice, one-minute author response. Preserve the repair block; split the five-minute peer recheck into about 100 seconds per project.
:::

---

## The author decides how to respond

| Response | What to record |
|---|---|
| **Accept** | The advice fits; I will make this change. |
| **Adapt** | The concern is valid; this other check addresses it better. |
| **Defer** | It needs more time/data; the claim stays qualified or pending. |
| **Reject** | The advice does not fit the evidence or scope; here is why. |

::: {.reflection-card}
Locate the disagreement. Preserve the concern and your reasoning, including advice you did not follow.
:::

This contributes to the existing A4 Feedback + Revision Ledger. It is not an additional graded assignment.

---

## Prioritise the consequence of the gap

| Priority | Why it matters | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | Could reverse or invalidate the main recommendation | Wrong units, missing input, unsupported threshold |
| **Important** | Limits confidence or who can use the result | Untested condition, unclear method or source |
| **Polish** | Improves readability without changing the conclusion | Label alignment or consistent colours |

::: {.ask-room}
Which fix most changes what someone is justified in doing with your work?
:::

Explain the priority for this project. A missing unit can be a critical error, not a cosmetic label problem.

---

## Perform one check or revision

[Session 2 · 18-minute repair block]{.kicker}

Before starting, write: **I expect ___; if I observe ___, I will change ___.**

- **Claim/figure route:** trace a value, correct a label, narrow a claim, or draw the missing comparison.
- **Existing tool route:** rerun one case, change one input, or test a GH/Python component against a known result.

Save the input, action, observed result and judgment. Keep the check small enough to finish or diagnose here.

::: {.warning-card}
If blocked, save the exact failing step and next check. A proposed test is not a completed verification.
:::

---

## Recheck the changed work

[2½ minutes per project]{.kicker}

Inspect the revised artifact and saved check, alongside the author's explanation.

1. What changed in the claim, evidence or rule?
2. Does the recorded result address the original concern?
3. What is supported now, and what remains uncertain?

::: {.activity-card}
“I accepted/adapted/deferred/rejected ___ because ___. I changed ___. The check showed ___; ___ remains unresolved.”
:::

Save one dated ledger entry. A4 requires at least three entries across the project; today's entry contributes to that total.

---

## Carry the revision into A4

| Required component | What today's review can improve |
|---|---|
| Practice Case · 2 slides | Recommendation, design action and limit |
| Research Brief · 2 pages | Method rationale, evidence and uncertainty |
| Object Card · 1 page | Figure, comparison rule and readable claim |
| Reproducibility Capsule | Runnable artifact, inputs, instructions and expected output |
| Feedback + Revision Ledger · ≥3 entries | Advice, response, change and reason |
| Reflection Note · 1 page | What changed and what can transfer |

::: {.source-note}
[A4 brief](../assignments/assignment-04.qmd) · [Final checklist](../templates/final-package-checklist.md). Screenshots can explain a result; the capsule must also contain the runnable workflow.
:::

---

## Reconstruct your review in four steps

**Object: your judgment as reviewer and your response as author.**

::: {.recall-4step}
::: {.step}
**Did** Which claim did I inspect, and what did I advise?
:::
::: {.step}
**Assumed** Which criterion or threshold did my advice depend on?
:::
::: {.step}
**Risk** What was missing, or what could change my judgment?
:::
::: {.step}
**Verify** What did the check establish, and what is pending?
:::
:::

Save this with your review card or ledger entry; share through Slack if available. This is formative work feeding the existing A4 package.

---

## Leave with a review and an evidenced response

::: {.activity-card}
**Reviewer:** “My judgment was ___, based on criterion ___ and evidence ___.”

**Author:** “I responded by ___; the observed result was ___; the remaining limit is ___.”
:::

Retain the review card, revised artifact or blocker record, and dated ledger entry. Before Week 11, resolve the highest-priority open check or state its limit clearly.

Week 11 tests whether another person can understand and reproduce the package you hand over.
